chunks: When he (peace be upon him) said this, in a long speech which we have mentioned its selected part in the collection of sermons,
two men from his companions advanced towards him, and one of them said: I rule no one except myself and my brother,
So, order us with your command, O Commander of the Faithful, and we will accomplish it for him.
Thereupon, he (peace be upon him) said: How can you two accomplish what I aim at?
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali mean when he asked his companions 'How can you two accomplish what I aim at?'
ai.summary: In this poignant passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) highlights the structural limitation of his authority during the Caliphate, where his companions could only mobilize their own tribes and families rather than commanding the broader populace. This rhetorical question underscores the gap between the spiritual mandate of the Imamate and the political reality of fragmented tribal loyalty, a key theme in Shia historiography regarding the transition from the Prophet's era to the Umayyad dominance.

en.sayed-ali-raza: The narrator says: When Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, uttered this during his long speech which we have included in the collection of sermons (No. 27),
two men from his companions advanced towards him and one of them said : I rule no one except myself and my brother (Qur’ān, 5:25).
So, order us with your command, O’ Amīr al-mu’minīn and we will accomplish it.
Thereupon, Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said: How can you two accomplish what I aim at?
